---
title: "Stacking, labels and features"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.2, message = FALSE)
```

A style is a stack of layers: background, water, roads, labels and so on.
basemapper can draw only some of them, and can stack several styles into
one map. Filters belong to a style: `style(source, features =, layers =)`.

```{r}
library(basemapper)
slc <- c(-111.8887, 40.7556)
view <- function(style) basemap(style, center = slc, zoom = 12.4, width = 720, height = 405)
```

## What a style draws

`list_layers()` lists a style's layers in drawing order, with the vector
tile layer each one draws (`source_layer`) and the *feature* it shows:

```{r}
l <- list_layers("OpenFreeMap.Liberty")
nrow(l)
head(l, 10)
table(l$feature)
```

## Labels

Labels are a feature like the others: `"-labels"` drops them (text and
icons), `"labels"` keeps only them, on a transparent background, to go over
another map.

```{r}
view(style("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", features = "-labels"))
```

## Stacking

A list of styles is drawn bottom to top, and each style has its own filters.
Satellite imagery under a vector basemap's labels:

```{r}
hybrid <- list("Esri.WorldImagery", style("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", features = "labels"))
view(hybrid)
```

ArcGIS basemaps are often published as separate services, drawn in order.
The Utah Geospatial Resource Center's *Lite* basemap is a hillshade, a base
map and labels; its catalogue name is one style that stands for the three:

```{r}
basemap("UGRC.Lite", center = c(-111.75, 40.62), zoom = 10.5, width = 720, height = 405)
```

Its filters treat the three services as one map: without labels, the labels
service drops out, and the base map's own labels go too.

```{r}
basemap(style("UGRC.Lite", features = "-labels"), center = c(-111.75, 40.62), zoom = 10.5,
        width = 720, height = 405)
```

## Features

`features` keeps or drops parts of the map by what they show: background,
water, landcover, parks, buildings, roads, rail, boundaries, places, poi,
terrain and labels. Plain names keep, `"-name"` drops, and the labels filter
combines with the others: `c("roads", "labels")` keeps the road labels.

```{r}
view(style("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", features = c("background", "water", "parks", "roads")))
```

```{r}
view(style("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", features = c("-roads", "-rail", "-poi")))
```

`list_layers()` of a filtered style lists what it draws, to check a filter
before rendering:

```{r}
list_layers(style("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", features = c("water", "parks", "-labels")))
```

## Layers

Features are sorted from each layer's source layer, as a convenience. For
exact control, `layers` keeps layers by id, or drops them with `"-"`; `*`
and `?` are wildcards:

```{r}
view(style("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", layers = c("-road_*", "-bridge_*", "-tunnel_*")))
```

A name that matches no layer is a warning when the map is rendered, so a
typo does not go unnoticed:

```{r}
m <- view(style("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", layers = "-lable_village"))
img <- render(m)
```

## In plots

Plots take the same styles:

```{r, fig.alt = "North Carolina's county outlines over Esri's shaded relief, with OpenFreeMap Liberty's water in blue on top: mountain ridges in the west; lakes, rivers, the sounds and the Atlantic in the east."}
library(ggplot2)
nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)

relief_water <- list("Esri.WorldShadedRelief", style("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", features = c("water", "-labels")))

ggplot(nc) +
  basemap(relief_water) +
  geom_sf(fill = NA, colour = "grey15", linewidth = 0.25) +
  theme_void()
```
